title: _PREFERENCE_RE has no trailing word boundary on the verb alternation — past-tense forms ('I wanted', 'I used', 'We used', 'I liked', 'I needed') fire the present-tense preference branch
location: _PREFERENCE_RE (lines 91-97), applied in extract_proposals at line 315
description: The regex group r"\b(i (prefer|like|love|hate|avoid|always|never|usually|want|need|use)|...|we (use|prefer|avoid|always|never)...)" is word-boundary anchored on the LEFT (the docstring explicitly says "so 'my' doesn't fire inside 'myself'") but the verb alternation has no right-side \b. So 'i want' matches inside 'I wanted', 'i use' inside 'I used', 'i need' inside 'I needed', 'i like' inside 'I liked', 'we use' inside 'We used'. The result: the politeness preamble 'I wanted to ask whether ...' (a disguised question), one-off war-story narration ('We used a workaround for the missing index until upstream fixed it.', 'I needed about an hour to track down the race condition.'), and historical past-tense statements are all queued as durable user-inference proposals. These phrasings are among the most common openings in real developer chat, so the noise rate on the review surface is high — exactly what the 'precision over recall' contract says it must avoid.
example_input: I wanted to ask whether we should pin the Docker base image in CI.
expected: No proposal — 'I wanted to ask ...' is a question preamble, not a durable preference; past-tense narration ('We used a workaround ...') is run-local war story, not setup fact
actual: Both sentences are queued as user-inference proposals verbatim ('I wanted to ask whether we should pin the Docker base image in CI.' and 'We used a workaround for the missing index until upstream fixed it.')

Severity medium, not high: proposals are inert (review-gated, never auto-written to the store; a bad one costs one dismissal), so no memory corruption — but the noise is routine-frequency on the review surface and can crowd real captures out of

In src/bettermemory/proposals.py, add a trailing \b after each verb alternation group in _PREFERENCE_RE (the 'my '/'our ' and contraction branches already have effective right boundaries):

_PREFERENCE_RE = re.compile(
    r"\b(i (?:prefer|like|love|hate|avoid|always|never|usually|want|need|use)\b"

title: Keyword scorer: unbounded body TF beats the 2x-capped coverage multiplier — a 1-of-3-terms memory outranks the full-coverage match and tops hybrid mode too
location: score_memory (lines 365-416; raw accumulation at 394-401, coverage multiplier `raw * (0.5 + 0.5 * coverage)` at lines 408-409) + _hybrid_fuse created-desc tiebreak (lines 750-755)
description: score_memory's coverage multiplier (0.5 + 0.5*coverage) spans only 2x, but the raw term-frequency sum is unbounded — so the code comment's claim ('keeps \"foo bar\" ranked above \"foo foo foo\"') fails as soon as one query term repeats naturally. For a 3-token query, a memory repeating one term >=5 times beats a memory matching all 3 terms once; for a 2-token query the flip point is just 3 repeats. Topic-focused memory bodies (a docker cheat-sheet, an nginx config note) repeat their headline word 5-7 times routinely. In mode='keyword' (the DESC-recommended mode 'for literal-token queries') the off-topic memory is rank 1 with relevance 'low' and the exactly-on-topic 'high' hit is buried at rank 2. The damage leaks into the default hybrid mode: keyword ranks A>B, BM25 ranks B>A, RRF ties exactly (1/61+1/62 each), and the created-desc tiebreaker hands rank 1 to whichever was written more recently — so a fresher cheat-sheet beats the on-topic fact in the shipped default ranker as well.
example_input: Memory A (1 day old): 'Docker cheatsheet: docker compose v2 is invoked as docker compose, not docker-compose. Install docker via colima; the docker daemon socket lives at ~/.colima/docker.sock.' Memory B (30 days old): 'Homelab containers: docker stack uses restart policy unless-stopped on every service.' Query: 'docker restart policy'.
expected: B (matches all 3 query terms, relevance 'high') ranks first in both keyword and hybrid modes; A is a partial 'low' match below it.
actual: keyword mode: A first (score 5.12, relevance 'low', match_terms ['docker']) above B (score 3.11, 'high', all 3 terms). hybrid mode: exact RRF tie 0.0325 vs 0.0325, broken by created — newer A wins rank 1.
verifier_notes: Confirmed despite adversarial stance. (1) Repro reproduces byte-for-byte: keyword mode ranks the 1-of-3-terms 'docker' cheat-sheet (score 5.118, relevance 'low') above the full-coverage 'high' match (3.1104); hybrid produces an exact RRF tie (1/61+1/62 = 0.0325 each, structural whenever keyword and BM25 invert two memories at adjacent ranks) and the created-desc tiebreaker in _hybrid_fuse (search.py:750-755) gives rank 1 to the newer off-topic memory. (2) Not a documented trade-off: the module docstring (search.py:12-15) documents only the lack-of-IDF weakness; the inline comment at search.py:406-407 affirmatively claims the coverage multiplier "keeps 'foo bar' ranked above 'foo foo foo'" — I verified that exact pair fails: score_memory gives 'foo foo foo' 2.475 vs 'foo bar' 2.2 on query ['foo','bar'] (flip at tf=3 for 2-token queries, tf=5 for 3-token, as claimed). Intent-vs-behavior mismatch, and no test pins spam ordering (tests/test_search.py:287-301 assert relevance labels only). (3) Realistic inputs: topic-headline repetition of 5-7x is normal in stored notes, and keyword mode is the recommended mode "for literal-token queries" in the user-facing tool description (handlers/search.py:96-97). Severity medium, not high: relevance labels stay honest ('high' on the buried hit, 'low' on the spurious rank-1), expand_top only inlines 'high'-relevance top hits so it never amplifies the wrong memory, and default max_results=5 still returns the on-topic hit — the harm is ranking i
suggested_fix: Saturate per-term body TF in score_memory (search.py:397): change `contrib = body_hits + 2 * scope_hit` to `contrib = min(body_hits, 2) + 2 * scope_hit`. With the cap at 2, a body-only single-term spam memory tops out at 2 * (0.5 + 0.5/n) <= 1.5, strictly below any full-coverage match (raw >= n, multiplier 1.0) for every query length n >= 2 — making the line-406 comment's documented property actually hold. This also repairs the hybrid leak: keyword then agrees with BM25 (B > A), eliminating the structural RRF tie, so no change to _hybrid_fuse or the tiebreaker is needed. Mirrors the design already present in the BM25 scorer (k1 TF saturation) and preserves the module's conservative scoring: monotonic in distinct-term coverage, scope 2x weight untouched, recency untouched. Update the comment at search.py:406-407 to state the cap. Existing tests are score-label based (tests/test_search.py:287-301) and unaffected; add a regression test asserting score_memory('foo bar') > score_memory('foo foo foo') for query ['foo','bar'] and the docker repro ordering in both keyword and hybrid modes.

title: No stemming anywhere in the pipeline: plural/singular query inflections ('standups' vs 'standup') are a total miss in every ranker AND the FTS5 index
location: tokenize (lines 144-150, exact-token equality in score_memory line 395 / score_memory_bm25 line 340) + index.py FTS5 schema line 141 (tokenize='unicode61', not porter)
description: Matching is exact token equality after lowercasing — no stemming or lemmatization in the keyword, BM25, or hybrid rankers, and the FTS5 prefilter uses unicode61 (SQLite ships porter precisely for this, unused). So the most ordinary morphological variance between a retrieval question and a stored fact — plural vs singular — yields zero overlap: query 'standups' against a body saying 'Daily standup is at 9:15' returns NO hits in any mode, and the FTS5 index also returns nothing (so on a large store the candidate prefilter can't even surface it for a smarter ranker). Multi-word queries fare no better: 'standups schedule' returns zero hits; 'daily standups' survives only via the incidental 'daily' match (relevance 'medium' with the actual topic word reported unmatched). Users naturally pluralize when asking ('what do I have about standups / dotfiles / containers / migrations?') while bodies use the singular, and vice versa — each such mismatch is a silent retrieval miss the auditor then double-counts as the model 'not searching'. Distinct from the previously-reported separator-spelling finding (hyphen/snake vs space): this is inflectional morphology on a single plain word, no separators involved.
example_input: Stored memory: 'Daily standup is at 9:15 with the platform team; Mattias gives the infra update.' Queries: 'standups', 'standups schedule', 'daily standups'.
expected: The standup memory surfaces for the trivially-inflected query (any production search engine's default analyzer handles plural/singular).
actual: 'standups' -> [] in keyword, bm25 and hybrid; 'standups schedule' -> []; 'daily standups' matches only on 'daily' (relevance 'medium', 'standups' absent from match_terms). FTS5 unicode61: MATCH 'standups' -> 0 rows against the same body.
verifier_notes: CONFIRMED despite the refute-first stance. (1) Repro verified at HEAD: query 'standups' against body 'Daily standup is at 9:15 with the platform team...' returns [] in keyword, bm25, AND hybrid modes; 'standups schedule' returns []; 'daily standups' returns relevance='medium' with match_terms=['daily'] only (the topic word unmatched); singular 'standup' returns 'high'. FTS5 with the shipped tokenize='unicode61' (src/bettermemory/index.py:141) MATCHes 0 rows for 'standups' against the same body, while tokenize='porter unicode61' (built into SQLite, no new dependency) matches it. (2) Not a documented trade-off: grepped src/tests/docs/CHANGELOG/ROADMAP for stem/porter/plural/inflect/lemma — zero hits. The tokenize docstring (src/bettermemory/search.py:144-150) and the _expand_kebab design comment discuss separator handling at length but never inflection; the ROADMAP's recall mitigation is the extras-gated embeddings path, not the default install. (3) One mechanism refinement: for single-word total-miss queries on a large store, the empty FTS candidate set triggers the load_all fallback (src/bettermemory/_handlers.py:205-209), so the prefilter is not the gate there — the lexical rankers then miss anyway (identical outcome). But for multi-word queries the MATCH clause is OR-joined (index.py:519-522), so other memories matching the other term fill the 50-candidate pool, the fallback never fires, and the true hit is excluded before ANY ranker — including semantic in hybrid mode — ca
suggested_fix: Two-part minimal fix preserving the module's conservative, asymmetric design. (a) FTS5 layer: change tokenize='unicode61' to tokenize='porter unicode61' in _SCHEMA (src/bettermemory/index.py:141) and bump SCHEMA_VERSION (index.py:108) to force the documented one-time rebuild — porter ships inside SQLite, zero new dependencies, and verified to match 'standups' against 'standup'. (b) In-memory rankers (src/bettermemory/search.py): add a conservative S-stemmer fold (Harman-style: only alphabetic tokens >=4 chars; strip trailing 'es' after s/x/z/ch/sh, else trailing 's' unless the token ends in 'ss'/'us'/'is') and apply it ADDITIVELY on the index side, mirroring _expand_kebab's documented asymmetry — for each body/scope token also emit its folded form, and fold query tokens to the same canonical form at lookup, while keeping the original tokens so exact identifier matches ('k8s', 'ls', 'redis') are never lost. Mirror the same fold in compute_idf's body tokenization so BM25 document-frequency stats stay consistent with score_memory_bm25's lookups. Report the original (unfolded) query token in match_terms to preserve the field's contract. Add regression tests: 'standups' vs 'standup' body must hit in keyword/bm25/hybrid and via the FTS prefilter, and an identifier guard test that 'redis' does not fold to 'redi'.
